<b>Анатомическая позиция</b> — все описа: Anatomical position — all anatomical descriptions assume the person stands upright, looking forward, arms at the sides with palms facing forward, feet together. “Right” and “left” always mean the person’s own sides, not the viewer’s (so in a front view the right side of the body is on the left). Three mutually perpendicular planes pass through the body: sagittal (green), frontal (blue) and transverse (pink). Choose one to cut the body along it.

Three mutually perpendicular planes pass through the body.
<b>Сагиттальная плоскость</b> (от лат. s: The sagittal plane (Latin sagitta — arrow) runs front to back and divides the body into right and left parts. The only sagittal plane exactly in the middle is the median (midsagittal) plane; the others are parasagittal. Turn on “Move” — the plane will sweep through the body and you will see which organs it cuts. On MRI, sagittal sections show, for example, the whole length of the spine and spinal cord.
<b>Фронтальная плоскость</b> (корональна: The frontal plane (coronal, from Latin corona — crown: it runs like the band of a crown over the head) is parallel to the forehead and divides the body into anterior and posterior parts. On an ordinary frontal chest X-ray the whole body is, as it were, “flattened” into the frontal plane.
<b>Поперечная плоскость</b> (горизонталь: The transverse plane (horizontal; on CT and MRI — axial) is perpendicular to the long axis of the body and divides it into upper and lower parts. Almost all CT images are series of transverse sections; by convention they are viewed “from below”, from the patient’s feet, so the right side of the body is on the left of the image.
<b>Верхний</b> (краниальный — ближе к го: Superior (cranial — toward the head) and inferior (caudal — toward the “tail”, the coccyx). The heart lies above the diaphragm, the bladder below the navel. For limbs “superior/inferior” are avoided — proximal and distal are used instead. In the brain and the embryo “rostral” (toward the nose) is often used.
<b>Передний</b> (вентральный — со сторон: Anterior (ventral — on the belly side) and posterior (dorsal — on the back side). The sternum lies anterior to the heart, the spine posterior. On the hand the terms are palmar and dorsal, on the foot plantar and dorsal.
<b>Медиальный</b> — ближе к срединной ли: Medial — closer to the midline of the body (green vertical), lateral — farther from it, to the side. In the anatomical position the thumb is lateral and the little finger medial; the ulna is medial to the radius. The lungs lie lateral to the heart.
<b>Проксимальный</b> — ближе к месту при: Proximal — closer to where the limb attaches to the trunk (or to the start of a structure), distal — farther from it. The elbow is proximal to the hand, the knee distal to the thigh. The same words are used for vessels, nerves and the gut: the proximal small intestine is closer to the stomach.
<b>Поверхностный</b> — ближе к поверхнос: Superficial — closer to the body surface, deep — farther from it. Skin is superficial to muscle, and the femur is the deepest tissue of the thigh. Hence “superficial” and “deep” veins of the legs: a clot in the deep veins is more dangerous.
<b>Ипсилатеральный</b> — на той же сторо: Ipsilateral — on the same side of the body (left hand and left foot — green arc), contralateral — on the opposite side (left hand and right foot — orange). Important in neurology: the left hemisphere controls the muscles of the right half of the body — a left-sided stroke causes contralateral paralysis on the right. Bilateral — on both sides.
<b>Полости тела</b> — замкнутые простран: Body cavities are enclosed spaces that hold the organs. The dorsal (posterior) cavity is the cranial cavity and the vertebral canal: they hold the brain and spinal cord, protected by bone and meninges. The ventral (anterior) cavity is divided by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity (two pleural cavities with the lungs and the mediastinum with the heart in the pericardium) and the abdominopelvic cavity — the abdominal cavity and the cavity of the lesser pelvis. Choose a group.
<b>Дорсальная полость</b>: полость череп: Dorsal cavity: the cranial cavity (blue) continues through the foramen magnum into the vertebral canal (green) — one system filled with cerebrospinal fluid. That is why a lumbar puncture for CSF is done in the lower back, below the end of the spinal cord (L3–L4 level).
<b>Грудная полость</b>: две <b>плевральн: Thoracic cavity: two pleural cavities (blue) around the lungs — a slit between the pleural layers with a drop of fluid; if air gets in (pneumothorax), the lung collapses. In the middle is the mediastinum (yellow — its superior part): trachea, esophagus, great vessels and the heart in its own cavity — the pericardial cavity (pink). Fluid accumulating in the pericardium (tamponade) compresses the heart.
<b>Брюшно-тазовая полость</b>: <b>брюшна: Abdominopelvic cavity: the abdominal (yellow), with the stomach, liver, intestines, spleen and kidneys (which lie behind the peritoneum), and the pelvic (purple), with the bladder, rectum and reproductive organs. Above it is bounded by the diaphragm, inside it is lined by peritoneum; between its layers is the peritoneal cavity (inflammation — peritonitis).
<b>Области живота</b> помогают врачу опи: Abdominal regions help a doctor describe where it hurts and what can be felt. Following Netter, the abdomen is divided by two horizontal planes — the subcostal (through the lowest points of the 10th ribs, level L3) and the intertubercular (through the tubercles of the iliac crests, L5) — and two vertical midclavicular lines passing through the midpoints of the inguinal ligaments: this gives 9 regions. (Russian textbooks often draw the lower line between the anterior superior iliac spines and the verticals along the lateral edges of the rectus muscles.) The white dashed line is the transpyloric plane (L1): pylorus, head of the pancreas, renal hila. Simpler — 4 quadrants: a vertical and a horizontal line through the navel. Choose a region to highlight the organs that project into it.
<b>Правая подреберная область</b>: печен: Right hypochondriac region: liver and gallbladder. Pain here after fatty food is a typical sign of biliary colic; in cholecystitis the pain increases on inspiration while pressing under the costal margin (Murphy’s sign).
<b>Надчревная (эпигастральная) область</: Epigastric region: stomach, left lobe of the liver, pancreas, duodenum. Pain “in the pit of the stomach” — gastritis, ulcer; but a myocardial infarction of the inferior (diaphragmatic) wall — the gastralgic form — and appendicitis can also start here.
<b>Левая подреберная область</b>: селезё: Left hypochondriac region: spleen, fundus of the stomach, left (splenic) flexure of the colon. An enlarged spleen (in mononucleosis) can be felt below the costal margin and ruptures easily with trauma.
<b>Правая боковая область</b>: восходяща: Right lateral (lumbar) region: ascending colon; behind it the right kidney (the kidneys are retroperitoneal, on the posterior wall).
<b>Пупочная область</b>: петли тонкой ки: Umbilical region: loops of small intestine, transverse colon. Appendicitis pain starts here and later moves to the right inguinal region.
<b>Левая боковая область</b>: нисходящая: Left lateral (lumbar) region: descending colon; behind it the left kidney.
<b>Правая паховая (подвздошная) область<: Right inguinal (iliac) region: cecum and the vermiform appendix. McBurney’s point (red) lies at the junction of the outer and middle thirds of the line from the navel to the anterior superior iliac spine: tenderness is greatest here in appendicitis.
<b>Лобковая (надлобковая) область</b>: м: Pubic (suprapubic) region: bladder (when distended it can be felt above the pubis), in women the uterus, loops of small intestine.
<b>Левая паховая область</b>: сигмовидна: Left inguinal region: sigmoid colon. Pain here in older people is a common sign of diverticulitis.
<b>Правый верхний квадрант</b>: печень,: Right upper quadrant: liver, gallbladder, duodenum, right flexure of the colon, right kidney.
<b>Левый верхний квадрант</b>: желудок,: Left upper quadrant: stomach, spleen, body and tail of the pancreas, left kidney.
<b>Правый нижний квадрант</b>: слепая ки: Right lower quadrant: cecum, vermiform appendix (McBurney’s point — red), end of the small intestine, in women the right ovary.
<b>Левый нижний квадрант</b>: сигмовидна: Left lower quadrant: sigmoid and descending colon, loops of small intestine, in women the left ovary.

\n <div><h2>Язык анатомии</h2>\n:
The language of anatomy

All terms of position are measured from the anatomical position: the person stands, face and palms forward, feet together. Planes: sagittal (one of them is the median plane), frontal (coronal), transverse (horizontal, axial). Axes: vertical, sagittal (anteroposterior), frontal (transverse) — joint movements take place around them.

Paired terms

  • superior (cranial) — inferior (caudal);
  • anterior (ventral) — posterior (dorsal); palmar — dorsal; plantar — dorsal;
  • medial — lateral; intermediate;
  • proximal — distal;
  • superficial — deep; external — internal (for walls of cavities);
  • ipsilateral — contralateral; bilateral.

Cavities

Dorsal: cranial cavity and vertebral canal. Ventral: thoracic (pleural cavities, mediastinum, pericardial cavity) and abdominopelvic (abdominal cavity and lesser pelvic cavity), separated by the diaphragm.

<b>Трубчатая кость</b> (здесь — схема бе: A long bone (here a schematic femur) cut lengthwise. The shaft — the diaphysis — has a thick wall of compact bone, with a marrow cavity of yellow (fatty) marrow inside. The ends — the epiphyses — have a thin layer of compact bone and inside spongy bone: a network of struts (trabeculae) aligned with lines of stress, with red marrow between them. In adults blood-forming marrow remains in flat and short bones (sternum, ribs, pelvis, vertebral bodies) and in the proximal epiphyses of the femur and humerus. The articular surfaces are covered with hyaline cartilage, the rest with periosteum (through it bone grows in thickness and heals after a fracture). The white line is a trace of the growth plate (epiphyseal line). A nutrient artery enters through the wall. The frame on the diaphysis marks where the block of osteons comes from.
<b>Остеон</b> (гаверсова система) — един: An osteon (Haversian system) is the unit of compact bone: 4–20 concentric lamellae of collagen and hydroxyapatite crystals around a central (Haversian) canal with capillaries and a nerve fiber. Between the lamellae, in elongated lacunae, sit osteocytes (purple) — former osteoblasts walled into bone; their processes run through fine canaliculi connecting the cells to each other and to the canal — this is how they sense load. Transverse Volkmann’s canals bring vessels from the periosteum. On the outside, beneath the periosteum, lie the outer circumferential lamellae. Bone is 2/3 mineral (compressive strength) and 1/3 organic matrix, mainly type I collagen (flexibility).
<b>Остеопороз</b>: разрушение кости (ост: Osteoporosis: bone breakdown (osteoclasts) outpaces bone building (osteoblasts) — especially after menopause, when estrogens disappear, with glucocorticoid therapy, and with immobility. There are fewer trabeculae, they are thinner and lose connections, the compact layer thins (the marrow cavity widens), and the canals in osteons enlarge into resorption cavities. Typical fractures — femoral neck, vertebrae (compression), distal radius at the wrist. Diagnosis — densitometry; treatment — calcium with vitamin D, bisphosphonates, denosumab. See the “Calcium: parathyroid hormone and vitamin D” topic.
<b>Синовиальный сустав</b> на срезе. Сус: A synovial joint in section. The articular surfaces are congruent — they match each other, with only a slit holding a thin layer of synovial fluid between them. The bone ends are covered with smooth hyaline cartilage (blue) — it has no vessels or nerves and is nourished by the fluid; beneath it lies the dense subchondral plate, and deeper, spongy bone with red marrow. The fluid (hyaluronic acid + lubricin) is a lubricant: friction in a joint is lower than ice on ice. It is produced by the synovial membrane (pink), which lines the capsule up to the edge of the cartilage and forms recesses. The fibrous capsule attaches at the edge of the cartilage and continues into the periosteum; outside are the ligaments. Some joints contain intra-articular discs and menisci (knee, temporomandibular).
<b>Остеоартроз</b> — самая частая болезн: Osteoarthritis is the most common joint disease: cartilage wears and thins (with age, after injuries, with excess weight), the joint space narrows, bone beneath the cartilage becomes denser (subchondral sclerosis — a thicker white band), and bony spurs — osteophytes — grow at the margins. Movement is limited, there is crepitus (sparks), pain on loading, and brief morning stiffness. Treatment — exercise and weight loss, painkillers, and joint replacement when the joint is destroyed.
<b>Ревматоидный артрит</b> — аутоиммунно: Rheumatoid arthritis is autoimmune inflammation of the synovial membrane: it thickens and grows into aggressive tissue — pannus (red) — which creeps over the cartilage and eats into the bone at the margins (erosions — dark notches). There is more fluid (effusion), the joint space is widened, the joint is swollen and hot, morning stiffness lasts more than an hour; small joints of the hands and feet are affected symmetrically. Treatment — methotrexate and biologic drugs (TNF-α inhibitors and others).
<b>Подагра</b>: когда урат в крови выше: Gout: when blood urate exceeds about 360–400 µmol/L, needle-shaped crystals of sodium urate (white) precipitate in the joint fluid. Neutrophils attack the crystals, and overnight an attack of intense inflammation develops — most often in the joint of the big toe. Under a polarizing microscope the crystals show negative birefringence; in chronic gout nodules (tophi) form. In detail — the “Nucleotides and gout” topic.
<b>Шаровидный сустав</b> — шаровидная го: A ball-and-socket joint — a spherical head in a socket: movement around three axes (flexion–extension, abduction–adduction, rotation) and circumduction. The shoulder joint is the most mobile in the body (the socket is shallow), and so it dislocates most often. The hip has its head deep in the acetabulum: it is stronger and more stable, but less mobile.
<b>Блоковидный сустав</b> — валик (блок): A hinge joint — a roller (trochlea) in a notch: movement around one axis — flexion and extension. Examples: humeroulnar, interphalangeal joints of the fingers, ankle.
<b>Мыщелковый сустав</b> — два округлых: A condylar joint — two rounded condyles on almost flat facets: the main movement is flexion–extension, and when flexed some rotation is possible (two axes). The main example is the knee, the largest joint in the body; its surfaces do not match, so cartilaginous menisci lie between them, and cruciate ligaments inside. The temporomandibular joint is also condylar.
<b>Цилиндрический (вращательный) сустав<: A pivot joint — rotation around one longitudinal axis. The dens of the second cervical vertebra rotates in the ring of the atlas — that is how we turn the head to say “no”. The proximal and distal radioulnar joints rotate the forearm: palm down (pronation) and up (supination).
<b>Эллипсовидный сустав</b> — овальная г: An ellipsoid joint — an oval head in an oval socket: two axes — flexion–extension and abduction–adduction, no rotation. Examples: the wrist (radiocarpal), the metacarpophalangeal joints of the fingers, the atlanto-occipital joint (the “yes” nod).
<b>Седловидный сустав</b> — два «седла»,: A saddle joint — two “saddles” turned to each other at a right angle: two axes, and combined, circumduction. The main example is the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb: it lets the thumb oppose the other fingers — the basis of the human grasping hand. Osteoarthritis often starts here.
<b>Плоский сустав</b> — почти плоские по: A plane joint — almost flat surfaces allowing only small gliding movements in different directions. Examples: joints between the carpal and tarsal bones, facet joints of the vertebrae, the acromioclavicular joint. Each moves little, but together they make the hand, foot and spine flexible.
Кость — живая ткань прочнее бетона на сж: Bone is living tissue stronger than concrete in compression and lighter than steel, and a joint glides with less friction than ice on ice.
\n <div><h2>Кости</h2>\n <p>:
Bones

An adult has 206 bones: the axial skeleton (skull, spine, ribs, sternum) and the appendicular skeleton (girdles and free limbs). By shape — long, short (spongy), flat, irregular; sesamoid bones lie in tendons (patella).

  • Cells: osteoblasts build, osteocytes monitor, osteoclasts resorb; bone is remodeled throughout life (≈10% of the skeleton a year).
  • Growth in length — at the epiphyseal plate (cartilage), in thickness — from the periosteum.
  • Bone marrow: red — blood-forming, yellow — fatty.

Joints between bones

  • Fibrous: skull sutures, syndesmoses, gomphoses (teeth).
  • Cartilaginous: intervertebral discs, pubic symphysis, growth plates.
  • Synovial (joints proper): cartilage, cavity with fluid, synovial membrane, capsule, ligaments; sometimes discs and menisci.

Joint types by shape

Uniaxial — hinge, pivot; biaxial — ellipsoid, saddle, condylar; multiaxial — ball-and-socket; plane — small gliding movements in different directions.
